solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Green man gets gin cocktail and pieces of jewellery

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: An eco-warrior with a gin drink is somehow also acquiring jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' looks like part of the drinks scene but signals that GREEN MAN GETS GIN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the bands with stones given when a couple agrees to marry, items of jewellery.

clue.text: Raise points about large European tax

indicators.note: about means the two points go around the rest, one at each side

parts.note: E and E: two compass points, east twice
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a big European tax is being raised on several counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E...E around L, E and VAT, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up to a higher level, a plain synonym.

clue.text: It's said hands with elasticity make one think again

parts.note: give is the stretch or springiness in a material

indicators.note: it's said marks that the word for hands is heard, not spelt

parts.note: paws is a jokey word for hands

explanation.surface: A puzzling piece of advice about flexible hands making someone reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' applies only to PAWS, giving PAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cause hesitation or doubt, so someone stops to reconsider.

clue.text: Travel round south-eastern Falklands Green

parts.note: to go is to travel
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Directions for travelling around the south-east of a place in the Falklands.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: Goose Green is a Falklands settlement, so the answer is the word that goes before Green there; it fits the puzzle's theme of greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose Green, a settlement in the Falkland Islands known from the 1982 war, supplies the first word of its name.

clue.text: Make forcible intervention to demolish nice slum

indicators.note: demolishing knocks something to pieces, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Developers barge in to knock down a nice slum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to demolish' signals that NICE SLUM is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to force one's way into a situation where one is not wanted.

clue.text: Grapnels only partially hold

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Grappling hooks give only a partial grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' signals the letters hidden across grapNELS ONly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip in which arms are passed under an opponent's and pressed on the neck; full and half versions exist.

clue.text: Dress out of control beginning to rile film-maker

indicators.note: out of here means the dress lies on the outside of the control word

parts.note: a robe is a long dress or gown
a rein is a means of control

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of rile is used

explanation.surface: A frock that has run wild starts to annoy a filmmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is read as 'outside': the dress word wraps the control word, and 'beginning to' supplies the first letter of rile.
explanation.definitionFit: Rob Reiner is the American director of films such as This Is Spinal Tap and When Harry Met Sally.

clue.text: Woman (and not mother)

parts.note: nor means and not, as in neither this nor that
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A woman, specified as not being a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's first name, as in Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: Deer knocks up glitter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
raps are knocks, as on a door

explanation.surface: A deer bumps into some decorative glitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELKRAPS around.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter and to sparkle both mean to shine with flashes of light.

clue.text: Green unit backs taking flying bomb to America

indicators.note: taking means the turned-round word holds the bomb inside it
backs means the word for unit is turned round

parts.note: one is a single unit
the V1, written VI, was the German flying bomb of the Second World War
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A green military unit backs sending a flying bomb over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' gives ENO; 'taking' means it holds the V1, the German wartime flying bomb, written with a Roman one. 'Green' is the definition, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is the colour of jealousy, as in green with envy, so it can mean covetous.

clue.text: Country rejecting doctrinaire bilateralism to some extent

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the hidden run is read backwards
to some extent says only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A nation refuses a dogmatic two-sided policy, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' hides AIREBIL in doctrinAIRE BILateralism; 'rejecting' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a country in West Africa, founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: IT company, sometimes green

definitions.meaning: a major technology firm, maker of the Mac and iPhone
a fruit whose skin may be green, like a Granny Smith, or red

explanation.surface: A tech firm whose branding is occasionally green.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is often green-skinned, and the same name belongs to the Californian computer firm.

clue.text: Indiscretions on which toilet grows, so they say?

indicators.note: so they say marks that the phrase is heard, not spelt

parts.note: the stem on which a loo grows would be the loo's stalk

explanation.surface: A surreal image of a toilet sprouting on a plant stem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks what a toilet grows on: a loo's stalk, which said aloud runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless chatter that gives away secrets is a set of indiscretions, as in wartime warnings.

clue.text: Reportedly smell nothing green

indicators.note: reportedly marks that the word for smell is heard, not spelt

parts.note: an odour is a smell; in a non-rhotic British accent it is said like eau de
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Apparently there is no smell to the colour green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' applies to ODOUR only, said the British way with no final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Nil, French for Nile water, is a pale greenish colour.

clue.text: Moving book up with an oil supply

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for book is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: supply is read as supple, bending flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A book is published together with a supply of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOME to EMOT; 'supply' (read as in a supple way) rearranges AN OIL into IONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving speech stirs the feelings, so it is touching in an affecting way.

clue.text: Makeup in pure green

indicators.note: makeup means composition, how the letters are made up anew

explanation.surface: Cosmetics in pure green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makeup' rearranges IN PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit has not yet ripened, so it is immature.

clue.text: 4 admitted to post office, in short

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 4-down, meaning to force oneself into a situation

parts.note: someone admitted is let in

indicators.note: in means the post office goes inside the word for short

parts.note: terse means short, curt

explanation.surface: A cross-reference instruction about being let in to a post office briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like the idiom 'briefly' but splits: 'in' is the insertion signal and 'short' is the word that is cut open.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to step in between, to intervene, close to forcing one's way in.

clue.text: I'm sorry Paul came out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An apology because Paul came out, perhaps in a confessional sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PAUL CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase, literally 'through my fault', is an admission of guilt, an apology.

clue.text: We believe these are left in lettuce

indicators.note: in means the word for left sits inside the lettuce

parts.note: cos is a long-leaved lettuce, romaine
red means left-wing politically

explanation.surface: Followers claim some article of faith concerning leftovers in a lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is the political sense: RED, a socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements of faith are things believers profess; credo is Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Jeweller's erratic fashion

definitions.note: read as jeweller is, the possessive ending standing for is

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A jewellery house's taste in style is unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is a verb here, rearranging ERRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartier is the famous French luxury firm of jewellers and watchmakers.

clue.text: Oozes confidence and finishes in the medals

parts.note: a confidence is a secret, something told in confidence

indicators.note: finishes in means the last letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: An athlete exudes confidence and finishes among the medal winners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oozes confidence' reads as a phrase, but 'confidence' is the noun SECRET; 'finishes in' takes E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to discharge a fluid slowly, as glands do, so it means to ooze.

clue.text: Politician's contacts don't start dancing

definitions.note: read as politician is, the possessive ending standing for is

indicators.note: dancing means the remaining letters move about into a new order
don't start means the opening letter of contacts is dropped

explanation.surface: A politician's connections are not starting to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start' leaves ONTACTS; 'dancing' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot Nat is a Scottish Nationalist, a member of the SNP, so a politician.

clue.text: Scattered around Turkey in all directions

indicators.note: around means the compass points surround the country code

parts.note: the four compass points south, east, west and north, here in that order
TR is the international code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Something lies scattered right round Turkey, everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The four points come as S, E, W, N, with TR after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means spread untidily over an area, so scattered.

clue.text: Article is surprisingly down- to-earth

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters fall in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece turns out, against expectation, to be sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges ARTICLE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone down-to-earth is practical and sensible, facing facts as they are.

clue.text: Old king punches some getting cross

indicators.note: punches means the king's letters strike into the middle of the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in have you any?
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch hits a few people and becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: GR, Georgius Rex, is a crossword convention for an old king.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is a familiar British synonym for annoyed, irritated.

clue.text: Headdress loses an ordinary booster

indicators.note: loses means the word an is taken away from the headdress

parts.note: a turban is a wound cloth headdress
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A turban loses an everyday part that gives it a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes AN from TURBAN, leaving TURB.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbocharger boosts an engine's power, so it is a booster.

clue.text: Third unit with time to move up top

indicators.note: to move up means a letter in the word unit shifts upward, to the front in a down entry

parts.note: C is the third letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A third unit is ordered to advance to the top in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move up' shifts the time letter to the front, since in a down entry the front is the top; 'Third' is C, third letter of the alphabet. 'top' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a loose garment worn on the upper body, so a top.

clue.text: Naive girl regularly found in giant green cube

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: An innocent young woman is often found inside a giant green box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and so on letters of gIaNt GrEeN cUbE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an innocent young woman, especially as a stock stage role.

clue.text: President Green

definitions.meaning: a bright green cloth worn, in legend, by Robin Hood's men

explanation.surface: A head of state who is environmentally minded.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the US president Abraham and to a shade of green cloth made in that English city.

clue.text: Sort of blue with old greens here

parts.note: royal blue is a deep bright blue
and means with, together with
ancient means very old

explanation.surface: Describing a shade of blue paired with aged golf greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to golf: greens are putting surfaces, and this St Andrews club governs the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews in Scotland is a club full of golf greens, the sport's historic home.
